# Grouper

<!-- slot-head:begin (generated by tools/make_method_pages.py; do not edit) -->
<div class="gp-chips"><span class="gp-chip">Seed-based · 5 methods</span><code class="gp-chip">--set grouper=</code><span class="gp-chip">28 options</span></div>
<!-- slot-head:end -->

The grouper looks at the neighbourhood of every seed in the frame of its approach direction and
turns it into one feature. The head predicts angle, depth, width and score from that feature
alone, so the grouper decides what the head can know about the local shape.

## Use it

<!-- method-options:begin (generated by tools/make_method_pages.py; do not edit) -->

=== "GraspNet-baseline"

    ```bash
    grasppanda compose graspnet_baseline/graspnet-baseline_pointnet2_g1b-realsense_18e \
        --set grouper=roi-grid -o graspnet-baseline_roi-grid.yaml
    grasppanda compose graspnet_baseline/graspnet-baseline_pointnet2_g1b-realsense_18e --list grouper
    ```

=== "GSNet"

    ```bash
    grasppanda compose gsnet/gsnet_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e \
        --set grouper=roi-grid -o gsnet_roi-grid.yaml
    grasppanda compose gsnet/gsnet_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e --list grouper
    ```

=== "Scale-Balanced-Grasp"

    ```bash
    grasppanda compose scale_balanced_grasp/sbg_pointnet2-transformer_g1b-realsense_18e \
        --set grouper=roi-grid -o scale-balanced-grasp_roi-grid.yaml
    grasppanda compose scale_balanced_grasp/sbg_pointnet2-transformer_g1b-realsense_18e --list grouper
    ```

=== "EconomicGrasp"

    ```bash
    grasppanda compose economicgrasp/economicgrasp_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e \
        --set grouper=roi-grid -o economicgrasp_roi-grid.yaml
    grasppanda compose economicgrasp/economicgrasp_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e --list grouper
    ```

=== "FineGrasp"

    ```bash
    grasppanda compose finegrasp/finegrasp_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e \
        --set grouper=roi-grid -o finegrasp_roi-grid.yaml
    grasppanda compose finegrasp/finegrasp_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e --list grouper
    ```

The first command writes a checked config; the second lists every option of the slot under that method, with what was measured. Then `grasppanda probe <file>` tries the config on real frames and `grasppanda train <file>` trains it ([Swap a component](../get_started/swap.md)). Each method page lists the same: [GraspNet-baseline](../methods/graspnet_baseline.md#grouper) · [GSNet](../methods/gsnet.md#grouper) · [Scale-Balanced-Grasp](../methods/scale_balanced_grasp.md#grouper) · [EconomicGrasp](../methods/economicgrasp.md#grouper) · [FineGrasp](../methods/finegrasp.md#grouper).

## Choosing

- **Match the head.** A grouper returns one feature per seed or one per depth bin (the two
  tabs above), and the head must read the same; compose inserts `depth-embed` or `depth-pool`
  where they differ, and says so.
- **The shape of the crop.** A cylinder along the approach axis is what the ported methods
  use; `ball` has no axis, `box` is a cylinder with a square section, `knn` follows the seed
  density.
- **Keep where a feature was found.** `roi-grid` and `roi-aware` pool the cells of a
  gripper-aligned box instead of taking one maximum over the crop.
- **Several radii:** `multi-scale-linear` fuses four crops with one linear layer,
  `multi-scale` with attention.
- **Sizes belong to the seed density.** A crop among the seeds sees the seeds of the proposal;
  after changing one, check the other.

## Details

??? note "The five steps of a crop"

    Every published crop is the same five steps, and almost every option replaces one of them.

    | Step | What the ported methods do | What the options add |
    |---|---|---|
    | query: which points, in which shape | a cylinder along the approach axis | ball, k nearest, oriented box, grid of balls, grid of cells |
    | geometry of a neighbour | offset in the crop frame | the same with its length |
    | encoder per neighbour | shared MLP (plus self-attention in EconomicGrasp) | DGCNN edge feature, PointNeXt inverted residual, layers of PyTorch Geometric |
    | pooling | maximum | mean, attentive pooling, vector attention, all with a padding mask |
    | fusion, residual | attention over radii (FineGrasp), linear + gate (Scale-Balanced-Grasp) | linear, max or mean over radii; a projected seed residual |

??? note "Input and output"

    ```python
    class Grouper(nn.Module):
        support: ClassVar[Literal["seeds", "scene"]]   # which points are grouped
        out_axes: ClassVar[tuple[str, ...]]            # ("seed", "channel") or ("seed", "depth", "channel")
        out_channels: int                              # width of the returned feature
        uses_seed_features: bool = False               # forward takes the seed features too

        def forward(self, support, centres, rotation[, seed_feats]) -> GroupFeatures: ...
    ```

    | | |
    |---|---|
    | `support` | points `(N, 3)` in metres, camera frame, with features `(N, C)`. With `support = "seeds"` the seeds of the batch; with `support = "scene"` the whole scene cloud, with zero feature channels under a sub-sampling encoder. |
    | `centres` | `(M, 3)` crop centre per seed: the seed at inference, the centre the assigner chose in training (so a crop may be empty). |
    | `rotation` | `(M, 3, 3)` crop frame; column 0 is the approach axis. In training it may be a reflection: do not assume a right-handed frame. |
    | returns | `GroupFeatures`: `(M, out_channels)` or `(M, D, out_channels)`, one row per seed. |

    What `grasppanda compose` checks before anything is built:

    - **`out_axes` equals the head's `in_axes`.** An axis is never added or squeezed
      implicitly; `depth-embed` and `depth-pool` do it explicitly.
    - **One depth entry per depth bin of the head**: the length of `hmax`, or `num_depth`,
      equals `head.num_depth`.
    - **The width of the seed features** a grouper adds to its crops equals what the encoder
      returns (below).

    The queries return the first `nsample` hits in index order and repeat the first hit in
    empty slots; a maximum does not notice the copies, a mean or an attention would, so the
    groupers mask them.

??? note "The settings that matter"

    **`LocalGroup`**: shape, encoder and pooling are options (all 48 combinations are legal and
    unit-tested).

    ```yaml
    model:
      grouper:
        type: LocalGroup
        shape: cylinder          # ball | knn | box | cylinder
        radius: 0.05             # ball / cylinder radius, half side of the box (m)
        hmin: -0.02              # box and cylinder: ends along the approach axis (m)
        hmax: 0.04
        nsample: 16              # neighbours per crop (k of knn)
        encoder: mlp             # mlp | edge | invres
        pool: max                # max | mean | attentive | vector_attention
        mlp_channels: [256, 256] # the last width goes to the head
    ```

    `edge` tells the MLP how a neighbour differs from the seed; `invres` adds capacity after the
    pooling. `max` is robust to padding; `vector_attention` is the only pooling that reads the
    seed's own feature.

    **`DepthLocalGroup`** is the same over the scene, gathered once to the farthest reach; bin
    `d` pools the members with `hmin < x < hmax[d]`, so near bins hold fewer members.
    `seed_residual: projected` works with any encoder width.

    **RoI poolings** (`roi-grid`, `roi-aware`) keep where in the box a feature was found.
    `roi-aware` leaves empty cells at zero, so with 1024 seeds most of its 64 cells are empty:
    try `grid_size: 2` or `3`. `voxel-set-abstraction` reads the scene and returns one feature
    per seed; `scene_features: true` needs a dense encoder.

    **`PyGConvGroup`** hands the crop to a layer of PyTorch Geometric as a bipartite graph: the
    members at their offsets in the crop frame, the seed at the origin, nothing padded.
    `conv_args` passes further arguments, for example `--opts 'model.grouper.conv_args={heads: 8}'`.
    Another layer needs three lines in `PYG_CONVS` (`grasppanda/models/groupers/pyg.py`).

    **Several radii**: `MultiRadiusGroup` runs one copy of `branch` per radius and fuses them
    (`linear`, `max`, `mean`); `branch` is any seeds-support grouper with a `radius`.
    `MultiScaleGroup` is the same with FineGrasp's attention over the scales.

    **The depth adapters**: `depth-embed` computes a per-seed crop once and tells the depth bins
    apart by a learned embedding; `depth-pool` takes the maximum over the bins of a scene crop.
    They make a swap possible; no paper proposes them.

    No grouper has released weights. To start the other stages from a checkpoint of the method,
    use `runtime.load_from=<file>` with `runtime.allow_weight_mismatch=true`.

??? note "The width of the seed features"

    Scale-Balanced-Grasp's crop adds `sigmoid(W f) · f` of the seed feature `f` to its
    256-channel crop, so the encoder must return 256 channels. `DepthCylinderGroup` states the
    width it needs, and `grasppanda compose` compares it with the width the encoder declares.
    When they differ, compose puts `DepthCylinderProjectionGroup` in its place (the same crop
    with a linear layer in front of the residual) and says so; `--no-adapter` leaves the pair
    refused with the ways out. The composed model is then a variant of Scale-Balanced-Grasp,
    not the paper's.

    The projection is a class of its own on purpose: the config hash of a shipped config covers
    the constructor defaults of its components, so a new option on a ported class would change
    the hash of every config that uses it. `MultiRadiusGroup` beside `MultiScaleGroup` follows
    the same rule.

??? note "Code and licences"

    The `LocalGroup` and `DepthLocalGroup` parts are written here on `grasppanda.ops` from the
    papers (a few lines each; the official RandLA-Net code is CC BY-NC-SA and was not used).
    `RoIGridGroup`, `RoIAwareGroup` and `VoxelSetAbstractionGroup` adapt the pooling rules of
    [OpenPCDet@233f849](https://github.com/open-mmlab/OpenPCDet/tree/233f849829b6ac19afb8af8837a0246890908755)
    (Apache-2.0) onto `grasppanda.ops`. `PyGConvGroup` is a bridge to `torch_geometric` (MIT;
    extra `torch_geometric`). `CylinderGroup`, `CylinderInteractionGroup`, `MultiScaleGroup` and
    `DepthCylinderGroup` are the crops of the ported methods. No grouper has weights.

??? warning "Pitfalls met while building this"

    - **Padding and non-max pooling.** Empty slots repeat the first hit; with a mean or an
      attention those copies would outvote the real members. Use the mask `crop_members`
      returns in a pooling of your own.
    - **Empty crops in training.** The crop centre need not be a seed, so a seed-support crop
      may be empty. Its first slot then counts as the only member, so no pooling reduces an
      empty set.
    - **Do not add an option to a component that shipped configs use.** It changes their config
      hash, and every measured cell built from them stops matching what compose writes. New
      behaviour goes into a new class or a subclass.
    - **A bridge passes the config check without its library.** `PyGConvGroup` without
      `torch_geometric` stops when the model is built, with the install line.
    - **`knn` over the scene is short-sighted.** With 20 000 points the 64 nearest lie within
      about a centimetre, so the far depth bins of `depth-knn` see the same members as the near
      ones. Raise `nsample` or prefer a radius.
    - **Memory.** A scene-support crop holds `seeds × nsample × width` activations per layer
      (and per depth bin).

??? note "Not wrapped"

    | Candidate | Why not |
    |---|---|
    | DOGraspNet's offset crop ([code](https://github.com/huamo555/DOGraspNet)) | a non-commercial licence; the idea is `encoder: edge`, written here. |
    | CUDA extensions of OpenPCDet and MMDetection3D | compiled, not installed here, and they rotate about one axis only; the rules were adapted onto `grasppanda.ops`. |
    | Voxel RoI pooling (Voxel R-CNN), the multi-stride sources of PV-RCNN | they read intermediate levels of a sparse encoder; the grouper gets the final features only. |
    | Closing-region crops (GPD, PointNetGPD, REGNet) | they need the complete grasp pose, but the grouper runs before the head knows it; they belong to a re-scoring stage the skeleton does not have. |
    | Region patches of the image-to-region family (RegionNormalizedGrasp) | no licence file, and the seeds of this slot are points, not image patches. |
    | KPConv, PosPool, point-pair features, Set-Transformer pooling | not reached yet; each would be one more `encoder` or `pool` value of `LocalGroup`. |
